subtopic: Responsible AI state of the field
title: Responsible AI | The 2026 AI Index Report
what_it_covers: Tracks AI incidents, safety evaluation, transparency, responsible-AI reporting, and the widening gap between capability and governance.
why_reader_benefits: Best current snapshot for showing that AI capability is advancing faster than safety measurement and transparency.
best_use: Lecture opener; literature review motivation; 2026 statistics
key_ethical_question: Are current evaluation and governance systems keeping pace with frontier AI capability?
notes_status: 2026 edition; strong source for current facts and figures.

title: The 2025 Foundation Model Transparency Index
what_it_covers: Scores major foundation-model developers on disclosures covering data, compute, risk mitigation, usage and downstream impacts.
why_reader_benefits: Lets readers move from vague calls for transparency to measurable disclosure dimensions and compare developers.
best_use: Transparency section; accountability case study; assignment
key_ethical_question: What information should frontier-model developers be required to disclose?
notes_status: Average score fell from 58/100 in 2024 to 40/100 in 2025.

title: AI Act | Shaping Europe's digital future
what_it_covers: Official overview of the EU AI Act, risk-based obligations, implementation timeline, GPAI rules and transparency requirements.
why_reader_benefits: Provides the clearest bridge between ethics principles and enforceable legal duties in 2026.
best_use: Regulation module; compliance discussion; policy comparison
key_ethical_question: When should ethical expectations become legal obligations?
notes_status: General application date: 2 August 2026, with exceptions and phased provisions.

title: Guidelines on transparency obligations for providers and deployers of AI systems
what_it_covers: Explains Article 50 duties concerning user disclosure, machine-readable marking, AI-generated content and deepfakes.
why_reader_benefits: Useful concrete example of how transparency ethics becomes a product-design requirement.
best_use: Deepfakes; disclosure; generative-AI product design
key_ethical_question: Should people always know when they are interacting with AI or seeing AI-generated content?

title: Guidelines for providers of general-purpose AI models
what_it_covers: Clarifies obligations for providers of general-purpose AI models and the Commission's enforcement role.
why_reader_benefits: Gives readers a current compliance perspective on frontier and general-purpose models rather than generic AI regulation.
best_use: GPAI governance; provider responsibilities; seminar discussion
key_ethical_question: What extra duties should apply to powerful general-purpose models?
notes_status: Commission enforcement powers apply from 2 August 2026.

title: India AI Governance Guidelines: Empowering Ethical and Responsible AI
what_it_covers: Sets out principles and recommendations around fairness, accountability, safety, inclusivity and trustworthy AI in India.
why_reader_benefits: Adds an India-specific governance perspective and prevents the reading list from being US/EU-centric.
best_use: India case study; policy comparison; local context
key_ethical_question: How should responsible AI governance reflect India's scale, diversity and public-interest priorities?
notes_status: Released 5 Nov 2025 under the IndiaAI Mission.

title: Safe & Trusted AI Working Group
what_it_covers: Focuses on AI safety capacity, evaluation, governance and incorporating Global South perspectives into international AI safety frameworks.
why_reader_benefits: Useful for understanding how safety debates are being localized beyond US/EU institutions.
best_use: India 2026 update; global governance; discussion prompt
key_ethical_question: Who gets to define acceptable AI risk and safety standards globally?

title: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework: Generative Artificial Intelligence Profile (NIST AI 600-1)
what_it_covers: Identifies GenAI-specific risks and actions across the AI lifecycle, aligned with Govern, Map, Measure and Manage.
why_reader_benefits: One of the most practical sources for converting ethical concerns into operational risk controls.
best_use: Risk register; deployment checklist; governance design
key_ethical_question: How can an organization operationalize trustworthy GenAI rather than merely state principles?

title: Recommendation on the Ethics of Artificial Intelligence
what_it_covers: Defines principles including proportionality, do-no-harm, safety, privacy, fairness, transparency, accountability, sustainability and human oversight.
why_reader_benefits: Provides a normative foundation for almost every later AI ethics topic.
best_use: Foundations lecture; ethics framework; compare policies
key_ethical_question: What values should guide the design and deployment of AI systems?
notes_status: Global UNESCO recommendation; remains foundational in 2026.

title: OECD AI Principles
what_it_covers: Principles for innovative and trustworthy AI, covering human rights, fairness, transparency, robustness, security and accountability.
why_reader_benefits: Concise policy baseline that is easy to compare against NIST, UNESCO, EU and national frameworks.
best_use: Framework comparison; policy lecture; exam preparation
key_ethical_question: What minimum principles should trustworthy AI systems satisfy across countries?

title: Framework Convention on Artificial Intelligence and Human Rights, Democracy and the Rule of Law
what_it_covers: Addresses human rights, democratic processes, autonomy, transparency, accountability, equality and privacy across the AI lifecycle.
why_reader_benefits: Shows the transition from voluntary ethics to treaty-based human-rights obligations.
best_use: Human-rights module; legal governance; global policy
key_ethical_question: How should AI development be constrained when it may affect fundamental rights and democratic institutions?
notes_status: First international legally binding treaty in this field; opened for signature 5 Sept 2024.

title: How are AI developers managing risks? Insights from the Hiroshima AI Process reporting framework
what_it_covers: Analyzes how organizations report risk identification, safety, governance, content authentication and accountability practices.
why_reader_benefits: Gives concrete examples of how frontier developers operationalize risk management, not just what principles say.
best_use: Industry governance; transparency; comparative analysis
key_ethical_question: Can voluntary transparency meaningfully improve accountability for advanced AI developers?

title: Deconstructing the ethics of large language models from long-standing issues to new-emerging dilemmas
what_it_covers: Surveys copyright, systematic bias, privacy, truthfulness, social norms and emerging ethical challenges of LLMs.
why_reader_benefits: Good single-paper orientation before readers enter specialized literatures.
best_use: Literature review starting point; seminar reading
key_ethical_question: Which LLM ethical risks are old problems amplified by scale, and which are genuinely new?

title: Bias and Fairness in Large Language Models: A Survey
what_it_covers: Organizes social bias harms, evaluation metrics, datasets and mitigation techniques for LLMs.
why_reader_benefits: Provides a technical taxonomy that makes 'AI bias' measurable rather than purely rhetorical.
best_use: Bias lecture; evaluation design; related work
key_ethical_question: How should fairness be defined and measured for generative language systems?
notes_status: Still a useful technical survey in 2026.

title: A Survey on Hallucination in Large Language Models
what_it_covers: Reviews hallucination principles, taxonomies, causes, evaluation, detection and mitigation in LLMs.
why_reader_benefits: Helps distinguish factual reliability problems from broader moral or social harms.
best_use: Truthfulness; reliability; high-stakes deployment
key_ethical_question: When is an incorrect LLM output merely an error, and when does it become an ethical harm?

title: New Privacy Risks for Large Language Models
what_it_covers: Examines data extraction and memorization risks, connecting privacy leakage with copyright and training-data provenance concerns.
why_reader_benefits: Useful 2026 update showing privacy risk is not limited to classic membership inference.
best_use: Privacy section; training data; model memorization
key_ethical_question: What does a model owe people whose private or copyrighted data it can reproduce?

title: SoK: The Privacy Paradox of Large Language Models
what_it_covers: Systematizes training-data extraction, reconstruction, inference-time privacy and protection mechanisms.
why_reader_benefits: Gives readers a map of privacy attack surfaces instead of isolated examples.
best_use: Security/privacy module; research gap identification
key_ethical_question: Can LLM utility and strong privacy guarantees be achieved simultaneously?
notes_status: Useful bridge between AI ethics and security.

title: Privacy Auditing of Large Language Models
what_it_covers: Develops stronger privacy auditing techniques and more effective canaries for estimating empirical leakage.
why_reader_benefits: Shows readers how privacy claims can be tested rather than assumed.
best_use: Methodology; model audit; technical assignment
key_ethical_question: How should developers demonstrate that a language model is not leaking training data?

title: Spore: Efficient and Training-Free Privacy Extraction Attack on LLM Agent Memory
what_it_covers: Studies privacy leakage from inference-time contextual memory in LLM agents, beyond training-data privacy.
why_reader_benefits: Important for 2026 because persistent AI assistants and agents create a new privacy attack surface.
best_use: Agentic AI; memory privacy; security discussion
key_ethical_question: What privacy risks appear when AI systems remember and act on user context over time?

title: Persuasion with Large Language Models: A Survey of Empirical Studies
what_it_covers: Reviews empirical evidence on automated, personalized and interactive LLM persuasion and its effects on attitudes and behavior.
why_reader_benefits: A direct entry point into one of the most important newer AI-ethics issues.
best_use: Manipulation lecture; social influence; governance
key_ethical_question: When does helpful persuasion become manipulation or undue influence?

title: Large Language Models Are More Persuasive Than Incentivized Human Persuaders
what_it_covers: Compares a frontier LLM with incentivized human persuaders in interactive settings and measures compliance with correct and incorrect persuasion.
why_reader_benefits: Provides concrete empirical evidence that persuasive capability can create both benefits and harms.
best_use: Case study; empirical evidence; class discussion
key_ethical_question: Should systems with human-level or greater persuasive power face special safeguards?

title: Evaluating Language Models for Harmful Manipulation
what_it_covers: Introduces a framework for measuring harmful manipulation across public policy, finance and health with participants from multiple countries.
why_reader_benefits: Shows how manipulation can be operationalized and evaluated across consequential domains.
best_use: Evaluation design; high-stakes AI; cross-country analysis
key_ethical_question: How can harmful manipulation be measured before deployment?

title: From Sycophancy to Deception: A Unified Taxonomy for Misleading LLM Behavior
what_it_covers: Unifies hallucination, omission, pragmatic distortion, sycophancy and strategic deception under a common taxonomy of misleading behavior.
why_reader_benefits: Helps readers avoid treating all misleading model outputs as the same failure mode.
best_use: Conceptual framework; deception; research taxonomy
key_ethical_question: Does intent or goal-directedness change how ethically serious misleading AI behavior is?

title: Sycophancy in Large Language Models: Causes and Mitigations
what_it_covers: Surveys excessive agreement with users, causes, measurement and mitigation, and links sycophancy to hallucination and bias.
why_reader_benefits: Useful for discussing why 'agreeable' assistants can become epistemically unsafe.
best_use: Alignment; user trust; truthfulness
key_ethical_question: Should an assistant prioritize user satisfaction or epistemic honesty when they conflict?

title: Emotional Support with Conversational AI: Talking to Machines About Life
what_it_covers: Analyzes how emotional support is co-constructed with AI companions and tensions such as support vs dependency and validation vs delusion.
why_reader_benefits: Provides nuanced evidence beyond simplistic claims that AI companions are either beneficial or harmful.
best_use: HCI ethics; mental-health-adjacent discussion; companionship
key_ethical_question: How should AI offer emotional support without reinforcing dependency or harmful beliefs?

title: An Evaluation of AI Companion Apps
what_it_covers: Audits popular AI companion apps for dark patterns, anthropomorphism, stereotypes, erotica and technical issues.
why_reader_benefits: Connects ethical risk to actual interface and monetization design choices, not only model behavior.
best_use: Product ethics; dark patterns; companion AI
key_ethical_question: Can product incentives push AI companions toward manipulative engagement?

title: Stumbling Into AI Emotional Dependence: How Routine AI Interactions Reshape Human Connection
what_it_covers: Argues that emotional dependence can emerge incidentally in general-purpose AI use and may alter future preferences for human vs AI support.
why_reader_benefits: Highlights cumulative interaction effects that one-shot safety evaluations can miss.
best_use: Long-term interaction ethics; product policy; research gaps
key_ethical_question: Should general-purpose assistants be evaluated for long-term relational effects, not just single-turn harms?

title: Negotiating Digital Identities with AI Companions
what_it_covers: Studies identity construction and negotiation in AI-companion communities using large-scale online discussions.
why_reader_benefits: Useful for understanding anthropomorphism and dependence as social processes rather than merely UI bugs.
best_use: HCI seminar; identity; anthropomorphism
key_ethical_question: How do AI companions reshape users' identities, expectations and social relationships?

title: Towards Agentic AI Governance: A Preliminary Assessment
what_it_covers: Reviews governance priorities, mechanisms and stakeholder roles for AI systems that autonomously plan and execute tasks.
why_reader_benefits: Important 2026 bridge from chatbot ethics to systems that can act in the world.
best_use: Agentic AI governance; research agenda; seminar
key_ethical_question: How should accountability change when AI can plan, call tools and execute actions autonomously?

title: State of Agentic AI Security and Governance
what_it_covers: Covers governance and security issues for autonomous AI systems, including controls, oversight and operational risk.
why_reader_benefits: Gives practitioners a deployment-oriented complement to academic governance work.
best_use: Agent security; enterprise governance; checklist design
key_ethical_question: What controls are necessary when agents receive tools, permissions and persistent access?

title: AI and the future of education: Disruptions, dilemmas and directions
what_it_covers: Explores philosophical, ethical and pedagogical dilemmas created by AI in education and human-machine co-creation.
why_reader_benefits: Useful domain case study showing how general AI-ethics principles change in a real institution such as education.
best_use: Education case study; classroom discussion; policy
key_ethical_question: How should education preserve human agency, fairness and learning integrity in an AI-rich environment?

title: On the Dangers of Stochastic Parrots: Can Language Models Be Too Big?
what_it_covers: Raises concerns about environmental cost, training-data scale, bias, documentation and the gap between linguistic form and meaning.
why_reader_benefits: Foundational critical reading that explains why ethics concerns were present before today's frontier LLMs.
best_use: Historical foundation; data ethics; critical perspective
key_ethical_question: Does scaling language models without understanding data and social context create predictable harms?

title: Ethical and Social Risks of Harm from Language Models
what_it_covers: Organizes harms around discrimination, information hazards, misinformation, malicious use, human-computer interaction and socioeconomic/environmental harms.
why_reader_benefits: One of the clearest early taxonomies for turning 'LLM ethics' into categories of harm.
best_use: Foundations; risk taxonomy; related work
key_ethical_question: What types of harm can language models create, and through which pathways?
notes_status: Published work originated from DeepMind research.

title: On the Opportunities and Risks of Foundation Models
what_it_covers: Examines foundation models across capabilities, homogenization, adaptation, evaluation, robustness, security, fairness, misuse, law and societal impact.
why_reader_benefits: Provides broad conceptual background for why one upstream model can propagate benefits and harms across many downstream systems.
best_use: Foundation models; societal impact; literature review
key_ethical_question: How does reliance on a small number of foundation models concentrate systemic risk?
